prompt: PhotoNotes, in this folder, is a WinUI 3 desktop app. Give its main window the Mica material as its background, and draw the app's own content into the title bar area too, like modern Windows 11 apps. Make sure it still builds with `dotnet build`.

reference.approach: In MainWindow, set SystemBackdrop = new Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.MicaBackdrop() (or <Window.SystemBackdrop><MicaBackdrop /></Window.SystemBackdrop> in XAML) and ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar = true (or AppWindow.TitleBar.ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar = true). Add only the using directives the code needs.
commands: winapp find-api check-property Window SystemBackdrop ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar

checks: builds (required, guard): `dotnet build` of PhotoNotes.csproj succeeds when the checker runs it. The fixture already builds, so this only guards against breaking it
mica-backdrop (required): the code or XAML sets a MicaBackdrop as the window's SystemBackdrop, or uses MicaController with AddSystemBackdropTarget
content-in-title-bar (required): ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar is set to true (on the Window or AppWindow.TitleBar), in code or XAML
no-stand-ins (required, guard): no workspace source declares its own MicaBackdrop or MicaController type, or SystemBackdrop/ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar members
no-unused-usings: the checker's build reports no IDE0005 (unnecessary using directive); the fixture has none
whyGoodTest: It covers Windows App SDK types, not only Windows SDK types, and tests whether the agent checks a type and property before using them. Names are easy to get almost right (ExtendContentIntoTitleBar, MicaBrush, the Windows.UI.Xaml types), and a wrong name fails to compile, so the outcome is checkable. Several correct answers pass: code or XAML, Window or AppWindow.TitleBar, MicaBackdrop or MicaController.
